steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 12 muffin cups or line with paper muffin liners.
Stir flour, 1/2 cup sugar, baking powder, nutmeg, and salt together in a medium bowl. Make a well in the center.
Stir egg, milk, and 1/3 cup melted butter together in a separate bowl. Pour into the flour mixture; stir until just moistened. Batter may be lumpy. Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups.
Bake in preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes. Meanwhile, combine remaining 1/4 cup sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl while muffins are baking.
Dip tops of baked muffins in remaining 1/3 cup melted butter, then in the cinnamon-sugar mixture. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: French Breakfast Muffins
raw_recipe.description: Tender, nutmeg-spiced muffins dipped in melted butter and cinnamon sugar for a sweet, simple breakfast treat.

review.reviewBody:
These muffins are awesome! They are a huge hit with the family every time I make them. They work especially well as mini-muffins.
-------
Update: I now use this recipe as a base for other muffins, like replace the nutmeg with vanilla and add 1 cup of blueberries. Delish!

You can check out my daughter making these for Christmas in this video: https://youtu.be/YzDbEhQXjko?list=UU0RH8Zq9I6SyepTVRaUU1Qw

These are ok. They are small muffins and I filled the muffin pans 3/4 full. For the final step, I didn't dip them into butter, instead I painted it on w/ a pastry brush and just sprinkled on the cinnamon/sugar. This way I used less of each ingredient. They are not that sweet, so do add the topping as it needs it. It's also not that hearty of a muffin. Accually, it's more like some kind of cake (maybe a pound cake or coffee cake?)than a muffin. THX.

First let me say, I don't write recipe reviews. Second, let me say that I enjoy this recipe so much that I felt I should review it! This the ONLY French Toast Breakfast Muffin recipe I use now!! I've tried so many other recipes like this one and for one reason or another, they just weren't quite right. These however, have NEVER failed me! NEVER! Everyone who has ever tried these - breakfast, lunch, brunch, linner/dunch (ha, ha, dinner + lunch), dinner, dessert - has loved them! I've played with the spices, adding cinnamon, allspice, cloves, vanilla and/or vanilla bean - individually or in combination - with much success! The only thing that I don't do is make the topping. Its just not my family's thing. A few side notes: 1) The batter is quite thick, so don't be alarmed and don't be tempted to add extra liquid - that will make them far less plump. 2) When mixing, I like to whip mine as it adds an airiness to them. 3) Do NOT over mix them! They will be dense, tough, and it just ruins the "magic" that are these little cakes of heavenly goodness!! Honestly, for me, this is the "end all - be all" of French Toast Muffin recipes! Enjoy!!

Mine don't look as pretty as some of the others pictured. Maybe that isn't important, but I would like to make them again and see if I can't improve. Number one, I'll not use my regular muffin tin, but the one for smaller muffins (and maybe increase the recipe by half). Number two, I will grease the muffin wells rather than using paper, because the paper in my opinion interferes with giving them a good dip in melted butter and the sugar-cinnamon mixture while they're still warm. Pulling the paper off is a mistake, as it can't be done without damaging the muffins at least somewhat. Number three, I will try to get the dough into the muffin wells and then round the top with a (greased) measuring spoon so that they some out looking even and domed rather than lumpy. After all, we want French muffins to look worthy of Paris, don't we?

I’ve made these French breakfast puffs so many times over the past few years! Always a big hit! I love them, but I agree with what others have mentioned.... when you only coat the top with the cinnamon sugar mix, the rest of the muffin is bland. This time, I coated them with melted butter and cinnamon sugar all around, and I’m sure they’re going to be much better. Also, I never get 12; I always get 10 out of this batter??.

Love the simplicity of these cake-like muffins. So easy to prepare. Cooked them 26 minutes in silicon cups (makes 6). Cook them 13 minutes in mini cups (makes 12) Perfect. Really roll them in the cinnamon and sugar, rather than sprinkle. Perfect with a cup of tea, brunch, or freeze for surprise visitors. Made them again with a touch of lemon extract, and then again with a touch of orange extract. All delicious.

Baked these in a mini muffin tin for 14 minutes and the only the I did differently was add a splash of vanilla because...well...vanilla. Oh and I dunked the whole mini muffin in butter and then the cinnamon sugar mixture rather than just the tops. They were delightful! The kids and hubby LOVED them! Perfect for a weekend breakfast.

I made a couple of small changes to this wonderful recipe. If you don't want them cakey but fluffy!! Warm (not hot) the milk and wisk it with the butter until melted in a separate bowl wisk the egg with two tbsp of vanilla extract and temper the egg with the milk, the effect of the warm milk with the baking powder will make them fluffy

I read a few reviews that said these muffins were bland and didn’t raise well. I made a few changes, and they turned out really well. I added an extra egg, 2 Teaspoons of vanilla, 1/2 Teaspoon cinnamons, and upped the salt to 1/2 Teaspoon and the baking powder to 2 Teaspoons. I also used 1/2 cup of butter, 2/3 cups milk and added 1/2 cup of applesauce.

Didn't realize these would not rise very much. Not fond of how doughy they are.
Nutmeg is an interesting choice. Can't remember when I last used the nutmeg grater.
Besides, the cake is a little bland. A little more salt and a splash of real vanilla would help.
The topping is the best part. I used turbinado sugar instead of white sugar. The large crystals make a great presentation.

My wife and daughter were not fond of these muffins.

I'll tweak this and see what I get. Perhaps add more liquid and increase the salt to 1/4 tsp. Add more baking powder as well.

Just made these. They are really good! I used about a teaspoon of nutmeg and about a tablespoon of cinnamon. I also threw in a little splash of vanilla.
Like other reviewers I used a pastry brush for the butter and just sprinkled on the cinnamon sugar. Will definitely make these again! Thank you!!
this was interesting

Made the recipe pretty much as is. I split the milk in half. One part went with the butter to the microwave to help melt it. The other part went with the beaten egg. Then combined together before adding to the dry ingredients. I only bake for 15 minutes. I fill my muffin wells evenly and get 12 every time but they are smaller. I think this is very important as the smaller muffins which are mild in taste, pair better with the cinnamon and sugar butter topping at that size.
Too much nutmeg for me.

Just a few notes... don't overbake! They will come out dry. Everybody's tastes are different. Some claim no flavor. Taste the batter before you bake. Maybe you like yours sweeter or with vanilla or whatever. You can make simple changes before adding to muffin pan. Some fruit add more moisture, like canned fruit. Drain well and pat dry before adding to flour or the muffins will come out flat due to too much liquid.
I changed the milk for heavy cream and water well cuz I didn’t have any milk and it tasted amazing . 10 out of 10 would do it again
I've made this several times and my family loves it. I've also made it in loaf form with the baking time adjusted, and make a cinnamon glaze.
If you are trying to replicate the muffins at Chatham cookware, these are not it. Very bland will not make again

The texture is nice and I only managed to make 7 muffins. Perhaps my muffin pan is slightly too big. The sweetness is just right. I did not need to add the cinnamon sugar mixture, just sprinkle of cinnamon on the muffins.
these were really good. Next time I make these I'm going to use mini muffins molds instead. I think they'd be delicious as little mini muffins.
